title: Arrest of glaucomatous ganglion-cell death when pressure is not the lever

concept.text: The proposed innovation is a treatment that durably preserves remaining sight in people whose glaucoma continues to worsen despite controlled intraocular pressure, without obtaining its benefit through an additional pressure reduction. Its biological target is the survival and function of retinal ganglion cells, the retinal neurons whose axons carry visual information toward the brain. The intended clinical outcome is sustained stability of the visual field, meaning the area a person can see, rather than a temporary improvement in a laboratory marker. The May 2025 editorial describes the clinical need for neuroprotection; it does not establish that this capability has been achieved.

Scope synthesis: this entry sets a demanding goal of arresting further glaucomatous loss in a defined patient population. A treatment that modestly slows deterioration could still be valuable, but would fall short of this proposed threshold. Arrest would preserve surviving visual pathways; it would not by itself replace dead neurons, reconnect lost axons, restore previously lost vision, or repair the eye’s pressure-regulating outflow tissue.

significance.text: A Vision Loss Expert Group analysis published on 2 April 2024 estimated that glaucoma caused blindness in 3.61 million people worldwide in 2020, with a 95% uncertainty interval of 2.81–4.42 million. It attributed 8.39% of global blindness to glaucoma, with an uncertainty interval of 6.54–10.29%. These are modeled prevalence estimates, not exact counts or annual incident cases. Scarce visual-field data and possible undercounting limit their interpretation. The IHME library page summarizes the same analysis and does not constitute independent replication.

Pressure lowering can arrest or slow glaucoma deterioration in most cases, according to the 2024 analysis. A durable treatment for eyes that continue to deteriorate despite pressure control would add a major therapeutic capability: preserving visual function when further pressure reduction is insufficient or impractical. The direct benefit would be prevention of additional loss, rather than recovery of sight already lost. The supplied evidence does not quantify how frequently patients progress at statistically normal pressure or after a large pressure reduction.

If effective and safe, neuroprotection could reduce the need to pursue very low pressures and could consequently reduce some patients’ need for surgery, a possibility raised by the May 2025 editorial. This remains conditional: a successful neuroprotective treatment would not automatically eliminate pressure management, work in every glaucoma subtype, or repair existing damage. The revolutionary significance depends on durable clinical preservation, not simply on identifying a promising molecular target.

missing_breakthrough.text: The missing capability is reliable clinical neuroprotection: interrupting ongoing glaucomatous injury strongly enough to maintain human visual function without relying on lower pressure. Crowston, Loreto, Sivyer and Bell’s May 2025 editorial described insufficient evidence to adopt potential neuroprotectants into clinical practice. That documents a translation gap between therapeutic promise and demonstrated patient benefit; it does not establish that every relevant injury mechanism is unknown.

Scientific synthesis: the original research identifies pressure-related biomechanics and vascular or metabolic stress as possible contributors to ganglion-cell injury. The supplied evidence does not establish their complete causal sequence, their relative importance in individual patients, or a single mechanism whose interruption would arrest disease. Developing this innovation would require an intervention that reaches the relevant cells, sustains a protective effect and remains safe during prolonged treatment. These are development requirements, not claims that a particular mechanism or delivery method has already been validated.

Two phase III memantine studies failed to significantly slow visual-field progression, according to the May 2025 editorial. This is evidence that those studies did not deliver the desired clinical benefit. It does not show that every strategy aimed at excitotoxic injury must fail, nor does it identify which alternative pathway will succeed. Likewise, an encouraging animal result cannot resolve whether protection will persist through the slower course of human glaucoma.

A further barrier is demonstrating arrest convincingly. Visual-field progression requires extended observation, and apparent stability must be separated from measurement variability, cataract effects and differences in pressure between treatment groups. The editorial anticipates several years of evaluation for nicotinamide and notes that enrolling fast progressors can shorten trials. Trial efficiency therefore depends on patient selection as well as follow-up duration.

current_state.text: In their editorial published on 23 May 2025, Crowston, Loreto, Sivyer and Bell reported that both phase III memantine studies failed to significantly slow visual-field progression. They also stated that no adequately powered glaucoma neuroprotection trials had been completed since those studies and that the large nicotinamide trials they discussed were recruiting. These are dated editorial assessments, rather than an independent examination here of trial datasets or registries. Recruitment is evidence of ongoing evaluation, not demonstrated efficacy.

The earlier research attributed a 48-month memantine result to a December 2018 Ophthalmology publication by Weinreb and colleagues. However, the retained material for that primary citation contained only a redirect, so the exact duration and abstract wording could not be verified from the supplied review. The 2025 editorial independently supports the broader finding that the two phase III studies failed to significantly slow progression. The access limitation does not demonstrate that the reported 48-month detail is false.

The earlier research also reported results from the October 1998 Collaborative Normal Tension Glaucoma Study: progression in 22 of 66 pressure-lowered eyes versus 31 of 79 untreated eyes in an intention-to-treat analysis, with P = .21, followed by a cataract-censored analysis reporting approximately 80% versus 40% survival at five years. No study text was available in the supplied review to verify those counts, statistical results, the meaning of survival or the cataract analysis. These figures remain an unverified account of that study and cannot establish the magnitude of residual progression here. Their absence from the reviewed evidence is not proof that they are incorrect.

Lu and colleagues reported improved visual function in a mouse glaucoma model and aged mice in a December 2020 Nature paper associated with OSK reprogramming. The reviewed abstract supports that animal finding. The accompanying supplementary discussion identifies the microbead glaucoma model as more acute than chronic, which limits its relevance to years of progressive human disease. The available main-paper material was a subscription preview containing the abstract and extended-data captions; a separate supplement provided the readable model discussion, although another part of its extraction was degraded. This evidence does not demonstrate multi-year, pressure-independent arrest in humans or establish a quantitative human benefit.

Evidence-horizon synthesis: the supplied findings establish the clinical evidence gap described in May 2025 and the reported mouse result from 2020. They do not establish whether subsequent trials, approvals or human reprogramming studies changed the situation by 1 November 2026. Accordingly, the proposed innovation cannot be presented as achieved, but neither can its continued absence worldwide be asserted as a verified current fact.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed demonstration: enroll a prespecified population with confirmed visual-field deterioration despite controlled intraocular pressure, then randomize participants to the intervention or concurrent controls. Demonstrate sustained visual-field stability in treated eyes and a clear benefit relative to controls over several years, with no clinically meaningful between-group pressure difference that could explain the result. Superiority alone would be insufficient because it could reflect slower deterioration rather than arrest. This is a proposed completion standard, not an established consensus threshold.
completion_criteria.label: Multi-year visual-field arrest outperforms controls without explanatory pressure differences

completion_criteria.text: Proposed measurement requirements: prespecify the visual-field progression measure, the maximum deterioration compatible with the operational definition of arrest, and the uncertainty bounds needed to support that conclusion. Specify pressure monitoring, cataract handling, treatment changes, missing observations and safety requirements before assessing efficacy. Biomarker improvement or structural preservation could strengthen the interpretation, but would not substitute for the required functional outcome. Visual-field stability would demonstrate preservation of function; it would not directly prove that every ganglion cell survived.
completion_criteria.label: Prespecified visual-field arrest criteria, uncertainty bounds and assessment safeguards

completion_criteria.text: Proposed reproducibility and practical boundaries: confirm the effect in an independent study or independently conducted cohort, document sustained treatment exposure and acceptable safety, and report the glaucoma subtypes, disease stages and pressure ranges actually tested. Results from an acute animal model alone would not qualify. Finite trials could establish durable arrest within their observed populations and follow-up periods, not literal universality, lifelong protection or exactly zero biological loss.
completion_criteria.label: Independent replication confirms durable benefit within reported clinical boundaries

completion_criteria.text: The multi-year horizon is consistent with the May 2025 editorial’s discussion of the time needed to evaluate nicotinamide safety and efficacy. Its observation that fast-progressor recruitment can shorten follow-up supports a practical qualification: trial duration should be justified by the ability to distinguish stability from continued decline, rather than treated as an immutable number of years.
completion_criteria.label: Follow-up duration distinguishes visual-field stability from continued decline

related_concepts.text: Roster-based synthesis: OPH-01, “Retinotopic reconnection of retinal ganglion cell axons to brain targets,” concerns rebuilding connections needed to restore lost signaling. OPH-10 concerns keeping surviving ganglion cells and their function from deteriorating. Protection could complement reconnection, but neither capability implies the other. The supplied OPH-01 title supports this distinction; its full requirements and evidence were not supplied.

Roster-based synthesis: OPH-05, “Patterned vision from the brain when the eye cannot send signals,” concerns an alternative route to visual perception when ocular signaling is unavailable. OPH-09, “Reopening of the human visual critical period,” concerns neural plasticity. Both could intersect with rehabilitation or restoration, while OPH-10 seeks to preserve the existing retinal output pathway. Their inclusion does not imply that brain stimulation or plasticity would prevent glaucomatous cell death.

Roster-based synthesis: OPH-08, “Reperfusion of established retinal capillary dropout,” overlaps with the broad interest in vascular contributions to retinal injury, but restoring capillary perfusion is a distinct capability from demonstrating pressure-independent arrest of glaucoma. OPH-11, “Prevention of progression from early or intermediate AMD to late AMD,” shares the goal of preventing future visual loss, but addresses a different disease process and progression endpoint.

Roster-based synthesis: OPH-02, “Biological reconstruction of foveal cones, RPE, and their blood supply,” and OPH-07, “One programmable repair for many photoreceptor and RPE gene defects,” target different retinal cell systems and repair problems. OPH-03, “Reversal of established cataract without removing the lens,” and OPH-04, “A manufactured cornea that clears vascularized stromal opacity,” address optical clarity. OPH-06, “A closed-loop control that sets axial eye growth,” addresses ocular growth. None of these capabilities alone establishes ganglion-cell protection. Cataract is also relevant to interpreting visual-field outcomes, so lens-related changes require explicit handling in an OPH-10 trial.

Scope synthesis: trabecular-meshwork repair and more convenient pressure-lowering drops, lasers or operations address pressure control rather than the defining pressure-independent capability of OPH-10. They remain potentially complementary approaches. This distinction preserves the identity of the present entry without treating useful improvements in pressure management as equivalent to its proposed breakthrough.

change_log.reason: Makes the proposed capability explicit and avoids implying that it has already been achieved.

change_log.change: Replaced the broad claim that the injury pathway is unknown with a clinical translation gap and clearly labeled development requirements.
change_log.reason: The reviewed evidence does not establish ignorance of every relevant mechanism or validate a single causal pathway.

change_log.change: Limited the memantine conclusion to the failure of the two phase III studies to significantly slow progression.
change_log.reason: Failure of one intervention does not establish failure of an entire mechanistic class.

change_log.reason: The primary memantine material was a redirect and CNTGS text was absent; preserving uncertainty avoids both unwarranted endorsement and unwarranted rejection.

change_log.reason: Clarifies attribution, evidentiary scope and the time boundary of trial-status claims.

change_log.change: Added uncertainty intervals and modeled-prevalence limitations to the global blindness estimates.
change_log.reason: Prevents point estimates from being interpreted as exact counts and preserves the analysis’s limitations.

change_log.change: Qualified claims about worldwide approval status, treatment exclusivity and developments through November 2026.
change_log.reason: The supplied review contains no subsequent evidence sufficient to resolve those current-status questions.

change_log.change: Expanded the mouse-result discussion to include the more acute model, partial main-paper access and limits of translation to chronic human disease.
change_log.reason: Preserves the demonstrated preclinical finding without treating it as evidence of durable human arrest.

change_log.change: Separated arrest from slowing and proposed operational bounds, pressure comparability, reproducibility and safety requirements.
change_log.reason: A superior treatment could still permit decline; completion requires an assessable definition of sustained stability.

unresolved_issues: Subsequent clinical results, regulatory approvals and trial recruitment status between May 2025 and 1 November 2026 are not established by the supplied evidence.
The CNTGS counts, P value, cataract-censored analysis, survival definition and five-year estimates require verification against the study text.
The exact 48-month memantine detail remains unverified because the retained primary material contained only a redirect.
The supplied evidence does not establish how frequently glaucoma progresses at statistically normal pressure or after specified pressure reductions.
The relevant causal mechanisms, responsive patient subgroups and a safe, durable intervention capable of the proposed arrest remain unresolved.
The acceptable deterioration bound, uncertainty requirements, pressure-comparability margin and sufficient follow-up duration are proposed design choices that still require justification.
Full records for related roster entries were not supplied, so overlap and distinctions beyond their titles remain provisional.

The review recommended removing inaccessible trial details from the proposed replacement narrative. They are instead retained as explicitly unverified historical reports because the user requested preservation or explicit qualification of unresolved quantitative detail; they are not used to establish efficacy or residual progression.

brief.title: Stopping further sight loss despite controlled eye pressure
possible: People whose glaucoma keeps worsening despite controlled eye pressure could preserve their remaining sight for years. A treatment would protect the eye’s nerve cells, which carry visual information to the brain, and stop further loss without relying on additional pressure reduction.
why: Lowering eye pressure can slow or stop glaucoma in most cases. Protecting nerve cells would give people another way to preserve sight when pressure treatment proves insufficient or further pressure reduction becomes impractical.
Such protection could also reduce some patients’ need for surgery to achieve very low eye pressure.

sources.quote: and reverses vision loss in a mouse model of glaucoma and in aged mice.

Crowston and colleagues’ 2025 editorial reported failed memantine trials and ongoing trials of nicotinamide, a form of vitamin B3. Lasting arrest of human sight loss remained a clinical goal.
missing: A treatment must stop further loss of human visual function despite controlled eye pressure, with benefits sustained for years.
Trials must distinguish genuine stability from test variability, lens clouding and differences in eye pressure.
Independent studies must confirm lasting benefit and acceptable safety during prolonged treatment.

milestones.label: Sight remains stable for years against a control group
milestones.explanation: A randomized trial would have to preserve the visual field, the area a person can see, for years and outperform controls without explanatory pressure differences. This would establish arrest beyond slower decline.

milestones.label: Clear measurement rules support a finding of arrest
milestones.explanation: A trial would have to set acceptable loss and uncertainty limits, pressure checks, lens-clouding and missing-data rules, treatment-change handling and safety requirements in advance. These safeguards would make stability credible.

milestones.label: Independent research confirms lasting benefit and safety
milestones.explanation: Independent research would have to confirm durable benefit, sustained treatment and acceptable safety across the patient groups actually tested. This would establish reproducibility and clarify who benefits.

milestones.label: Follow-up lasts long enough to detect continued decline
milestones.explanation: Follow-up would have to distinguish stable sight from ongoing deterioration in the patients enrolled. This would establish that apparent protection lasts long enough to support a finding of arrest.

uncertain: The causes of continuing nerve-cell injury and the patient groups most likely to benefit remain unresolved.
The acceptable amount of measured deterioration, uncertainty and pressure difference still needs justification.
The necessary follow-up depends partly on how quickly the enrolled patients would otherwise lose sight.

page.title: Pressure-independent prevention of glaucomatous visual-field loss
page.definition: A treatment prevents further measurable loss of the visual field—the area a person can see—in people whose glaucoma progresses despite controlled intraocular pressure. It protects retinal ganglion cells, the neurons carrying retinal signals toward the brain, without obtaining its benefit through further pressure reduction.

goal.need: Glaucoma left an estimated 3.61 million people blind worldwide in 2020. Drops and laser can lower eye pressure, yet in one cohort followed for a mean of 4.3 years, visual fields worsened in 42 of 179 treated eyes (23.5%) with every pressure reading below 18 mmHg. People who continue to lose sight at low pressures need a way to protect the optic nerve alongside pressure treatment. Preserving their remaining field would help them see obstacles while walking. Sight already lost would require a different treatment.

figures.caption: Estimated global vision impairment attributable to glaucoma in 2020
figures.note: Modelled prevalence, not annual incidence. Blindness means presenting visual acuity below 3/60; moderate or severe impairment means acuity from 3/60 to below 6/18.

statements.quote: Explore neuroprotection as an approach for prolonging RGC function and survival
statements.context: A research priority of the Glaucoma and Optic Neuropathies programme. RGC means retinal ganglion cell.

statements.quote: Methods to treat glaucoma other than lowering IOP/neuroprotection and non-IOP treatments.
statements.context: Seventh among ten research priorities agreed by eight patients and four clinicians. Stopping sight loss ranked first. IOP means intraocular pressure.

statements.quote: Better ways to stop sight loss/stopping progression of glaucoma.
statements.context: The final workshop of patients and clinicians ranked this first and explicitly included non-pressure-lowering treatments within it.

completion.title: A controlled human trial demonstrates pressure-independent prevention of further visual-field loss.
completion.criterion: In patients with documented glaucoma progression despite controlled intraocular pressure, a randomized controlled trial demonstrates prevention of further visual-field loss under a prospectively registered stability endpoint, superiority to control, and benefit not explained by additional pressure lowering. The protocol must specify the stability margin, confidence bounds, follow-up and pressure-comparability margin. Slower loss or a nonsignificant deterioration slope alone does not pass. No published numerical values defining this joint arrest test were identified.
completion.set_by: Technology Atlas; a goal-level fallback whose numerical pass/fail boundary remains unset.
completion.basis: The UK stability consensus addresses eligibility for primary-care monitoring. NAMinG compares visual-field sensitivity between arms at 27 months. In patients already progressing at pressures of 18 mmHg or less, mean sensitivity declined in both arms of a three-year citicoline trial. Brimonidine reduced progression events relative to timolol at similar mean treated pressures, with more drug-related withdrawals on brimonidine. These comparisons leave the numerical boundary for pressure-independent arrest in confirmed progressors unset.

milestones.title: A candidate protects against glaucomatous injury in animals with a statistically and clinically meaningful effect.
milestones.criterion: Demonstrate protection in an animal model appropriate to the glaucomatous injury being tested. Use enough animals to detect an effect that is both statistically significant and clinically meaningful. The workshop specifies no common effect size, sample size or follow-up interval.
milestones.set_by: Lasker Foundation/International Retina Research Foundation workshop, reported by Levin and colleagues; a published translational recommendation rather than a regulatory gate.
milestones.threshold_quote: studied in sufficient numbers to detect statistically and clinically significant effects.

milestones.title: More visual-field locations improve with treatment than with placebo at two-sided P < 0.05.
milestones.criterion: In treated open-angle glaucoma, use repeated 24-2 visual-field tests to estimate the slope of age-corrected sensitivity at each location in the study eye. Count locations whose slopes fall in the upper quarter of the pooled distribution. The mean count must be higher with treatment than with placebo on an independent-samples t test at two-sided P < 0.05.
milestones.set_by: Columbia University investigators, published primary analysis of the phase II nicotinamide–pyruvate trial NCT03797469
milestones.threshold_quote: Statistical significance was defined at P < .05 (2-tailed) for the primary outcome.

milestones.title: Visual-field mean deviation at 27 months is better with nicotinamide than with placebo.
milestones.criterion: In recently diagnosed early-to-moderate open-angle glaucoma, compare nicotinamide with placebo alongside usual pressure-lowering care. At month 27, visual-field mean deviation, a measure of sensitivity relative to age norms in decibels, must favor nicotinamide at the two-sided 5% level. Use the eye with worse baseline mean deviation and the protocol’s linear mixed model, adjusting for baseline mean deviation, pressure treatment type, time since diagnosis and baseline serum nicotinamide, with a random effect for site.
milestones.set_by: University College London, NAMinG protocol version 3.0, dated 18 December 2024, sections 6.1.1 and 9; written for early-to-moderate open-angle glaucoma.
milestones.threshold_quote: The difference between the treatment arms in VF MD at 27 months.

milestones.title: A candidate treatment increases survival of injured retinal ganglion cells in culture.
milestones.criterion: Compare survival of treated retinal ganglion cells with that of untreated cells exposed to the same injury in culture. A greater surviving fraction demonstrates protection in this assay. The workshop specifies no common minimum effect size.
milestones.set_by: Lasker/IRRF Initiative on Astrocytes and Glaucomatous Neurodegeneration, workshop recommendation for in vitro efficacy
milestones.threshold_quote: Once a treatment is shown effective in vitro

milestones.title: Citicoline slows visual-field loss over three years versus placebo in eyes progressing at controlled pressure.
milestones.criterion: With pressure-lowering care in both arms, demonstrate a slower decline in study-eye mean deviation with 2% citicoline drops than with placebo on repeated Humphrey 24-2 SITA Standard fields over three years. Eligible eyes have open-angle glaucoma, pressure averaging ≤18 mmHg over the last three clinic readings, and mean deviation declining by 0.5–1.0 dB/year on at least four prior fields during a period without incisional glaucoma surgery.
milestones.set_by: Omikron Italia S.r.l., phase III protocol OMK1P3, NCT05710198
milestones.threshold_quote: Difference in the rate of progression of VF damage in the study eye between the two trial arms.

not_found: No registered endpoint was identified that numerically defines pressure-independent arrest specifically in patients with confirmed progression despite controlled intraocular pressure.

results.finding: OSK reversed vision loss in a mouse glaucoma model after 4 weeks; sample size not stated in the source excerpt.
results.detail: The excerpt reports functional recovery but does not state the statistical significance of the glaucoma result or establish that cell experiments preceded the animal study.
results.quote: Fig. 3: Four weeks of OSK expression reverses vision loss after glaucomatous damage has already occurred.

results.finding: Nicotinamide–pyruvate trial: 32 analyzed; improving visual-field locations differed from placebo at P = 0.005.
results.detail: Median improving locations were 15 with treatment versus 7 with placebo after 2.2 months. Mean-deviation slopes did not differ significantly; sustained improvement or slowed progression was not established.

results.finding: In 32 glaucoma patients, mean deviation rates did not differ significantly with nicotinamide plus pyruvate versus placebo (P = .35).
results.detail: This was a phase 2 combination-treatment trial with a median follow-up of 2.2 months, not NAMinG's 27-month phase III endpoint.

results.finding: Four weeks of OSK expression reversed vision loss in a mouse glaucoma model. The sample size for the vision outcome is unreported.
results.quote: Four weeks of OSK expression reverses vision loss after glaucomatous damage has already occurred.

results.finding: Nicotinamide increased retinal ganglion cell survival at 3 days after axotomy in mouse explants (6 untreated, 6 low-dose and 11 high-dose retinas).
results.detail: Sample sizes follow the Figure 2 caption. Methods section 2.8 lists 6 eyes per group, including the high-dose group.
results.quote: This RGC loss and nucleus shrinkage is robustly prevented by NAM-supplemented media at a range of doses.

results.finding: Nicotinamide significantly reduced retinal ganglion cell loss at day 14 in hypertensive rats (10 untreated eyes and 33 treated eyes).
results.detail: The paper reports sample sizes in eyes for the cell-loss comparison. Nicotinamide started before pressure elevation, and the experiment measured structural outcomes over two weeks.
results.quote: NAM treated OHT rats demonstrated significantly reduced RGC loss and nuclear shrinkage in a dose dependent manner

results.finding: Nicotinamide reduced retinal ganglion cell body degeneration after axotomy in culture. Sample size and survival fractions are unreported in the supplied text.
results.detail: The text refers to supplementary Fig. S9A–B, which is outside the supplied excerpt.
results.quote: NAM robustly protected cultured retinas from RGC somal degeneration (Fig. S9AB).

results.finding: Nmnat1 gene therapy reduced optic nerve degeneration in glaucoma-prone DBA/2J mouse eyes (n > 40 per group, Fisher’s exact P < 0.001).
results.detail: The sample size refers to the optic nerve degeneration assessment. Gene therapy was administered at 5.5 months, and the model’s end-stage assessment was at 12 months.

results.finding: Pyruvate protected axotomized mouse retinal ganglion cells at 5 days in explant culture. Sample size and survival fractions were unreported.
results.detail: The text reports the direction of the explant effect and refers to Supplementary Fig. S3 for the underlying data.

results.finding: In mice with microbead-induced glaucoma, continuous OSK (n=10) sustained significant optomotor acuity improvement for 11 months.
results.detail: The year-long study compared continuous OSK with cyclic OSK and a nonglaucomatous saline group. Its significance tests compared acuity with the post-injury baseline. The study did not measure whether OSK preserved retinal ganglion cells or axons during that follow-up.
results.quote: Continued monthly assessment of visual acuity demonstrated the significant improvement in vision was sustained for 11 months

results.finding: In treated open-angle glaucoma (n=32), nicotinamide plus pyruvate increased the mean count of improving visual-field locations versus placebo (P=.005).
results.detail: Of 42 randomized participants, 32 completed the trial and contributed one study eye each.

results.finding: In treated open-angle glaucoma (n=32), short-term mean-deviation slopes did not differ significantly between nicotinamide plus pyruvate and placebo (P=.35).
results.detail: When both eyes qualified, the study chose the eye with better prior field-test quality. The Results give P=.35 and Table 3 gives P=.36 for the mean-deviation slope comparison.

results.finding: SPG302 improved pERG amplitude versus vehicle in mice with microbead-induced ocular hypertension (8 mice per group, P < 0.05).
results.detail: The authors describe the pERG recovery as partial. Pattern visual evoked potential amplitude and latency showed no significant differences.
results.quote: Notably, SPG302 administration significantly improved RGC function in MB-injected mice as evidenced by increased pERG amplitude compared with DMSO-MB, though no statistical differences were detected in pVEP amplitude or latency

results.finding: Cultured primary rat retinal ganglion cells (n = 3 biological replicates) showed 158.93% increased preservation with SA-2 versus vehicle after trophic factor deprivation.
results.detail: The assay normalized cell counts to the total cell count in the vehicle control group.
results.quote: At 1 mM concentration, SA-2 still demonstrated higher RGC preservation compared to the control in the TF deprivation model in primary culture and human explants.

goal.need = "Glaucoma left an estimated 3.61 million people blind worldwide in 2020. Drops and laser can lower eye pressure, yet in one cohort followed for a mean of 4.3 years, visual fields worsened in 42 of 179 treated eyes (23.5%) with every pressure reading below 18 mmHg. People who continue to lose sight at low pressures need a way to protect the optic nerve alongside pressure treatment. Preserving their remaining field would help them see obstacles while walking. Sight already lost would require a different treatment.". Reason: The current rationale gives the global burden but leaves out the frequency of further loss at low measured pressure and what preserving a field means in daily life.

add statement by European Glaucoma Society, 2024: "Better ways to stop sight loss/stopping progression of glaucoma.". Reason: The existing European Glaucoma Society quotation identifies the treatment approach but omits the workshop’s first-ranked goal of stopping sight loss.

edit completion: basis = "The UK stability consensus addresses eligibility for primary-care monitoring. NAMinG compares visual-field sensitivity between arms at 27 months. In patients already progressing at pressures of 18 mmHg or less, mean sensitivity declined in both arms of a three-year citicoline trial. Brimonidine reduced progression events relative to timolol at similar mean treated pressures, with more drug-related withdrawals on brimonidine. These comparisons leave the numerical boundary for pressure-independent arrest in confirmed progressors unset."; refs = [3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 15, 16]. Reason: The current basis omits the citicoline trial that enrolled the target patients and the brimonidine trial that compared progression at similar treated pressures.

add milestone after None: "A candidate treatment increases survival of injured retinal ganglion cells in culture.". Reason: The workshop identifies in vitro efficacy as the first experimental stage, but the current sequence starts with animals.

edit m1: title = "A candidate protects against glaucomatous injury in animals with a statistically and clinically meaningful effect."; criterion = "Demonstrate protection in an animal model appropriate to the glaucomatous injury being tested. Use enough animals to detect an effect that is both statistically significant and clinically meaningful. The workshop specifies no common effect size, sample size or follow-up interval."; threshold_quote = "studied in sufficient numbers to detect statistically and clinically significant effects."; threshold_ref = 8; refs = [8]. Reason: The title omits the workshop’s requirement for a clinically meaningful effect, and the criterion mixes animal efficacy with the outcome of one mouse experiment.

edit m2: title = "More visual-field locations improve with treatment than with placebo at two-sided P < 0.05."; criterion = "In treated open-angle glaucoma, use repeated 24-2 visual-field tests to estimate the slope of age-corrected sensitivity at each location in the study eye. Count locations whose slopes fall in the upper quarter of the pooled distribution. The mean count must be higher with treatment than with placebo on an independent-samples t test at two-sided P < 0.05."; set_by = "Columbia University investigators, published primary analysis of the phase II nicotinamide\u2013pyruvate trial NCT03797469"; threshold_quote = "Statistical significance was defined at P\u2009<\u2009.05 (2-tailed) for the primary outcome."; threshold_ref = 2; refs = [2]. Reason: The existing criterion reports participant counts and outcomes but leaves the published rule for counting an improving location unspecified.

edit m3: title = "Visual-field mean deviation at 27 months is better with nicotinamide than with placebo."; criterion = "In recently diagnosed early-to-moderate open-angle glaucoma, compare nicotinamide with placebo alongside usual pressure-lowering care. At month 27, visual-field mean deviation, a measure of sensitivity relative to age norms in decibels, must favor nicotinamide at the two-sided 5% level. Use the eye with worse baseline mean deviation and the protocol\u2019s linear mixed model, adjusting for baseline mean deviation, pressure treatment type, time since diagnosis and baseline serum nicotinamide, with a random effect for site."; threshold_quote = "The difference between the treatment arms in VF MD at 27 months."; threshold_ref = 7; refs = [7, 10]. Reason: The current title implies preservation from baseline, while the primary endpoint compares the groups at month 27 and the criterion includes transient registry information.

add milestone after m3: "Citicoline slows visual-field loss over three years versus placebo in eyes progressing at controlled pressure.". Reason: A registered phase III trial tests slower loss in eyes with documented progression at controlled pressure, a closer step to arrest than a single follow-up comparison in newly diagnosed patients.
